input: What did Snowflake say about consumption trends on its most recent earnings call?

output.question: What did Snowflake say about consumption trends on its most recent earnings call?
output.answer: On Snowflake’s most recent call—the September 2, 2026 Q2 FY27 call—management said AI adoption is lifting consumption across the broader platform: customers using AI consume more core Snowflake services, and CoCo adopters are consuming more of the core as well. Management said the acceleration was broad-based rather than concentrated in AI-native companies, with AI products contributing approximately half of the acceleration and faster migrations and other workloads contributing the rest. Snowflake said it is not yet ready to disclose the exact consumption uplift for AI adopters, but reported that newer customer cohorts are reaching 80% of purchased consumption more visibly and that it raised FY27 product-revenue guidance to $6.07 billion, or 36% year-over-year growth, based on observed consumption patterns. key_facts.fact: Snowflake said AI activation is increasing overall platform consumption and that customers using AI consume more across the data platform.
CFO Brian Robins said CoCo accounts are consuming more of Snowflake’s core platform, describing a flywheel effect; Snowflake had 9,100 CoCo accounts in the quarter.
CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy said AI products contributed approximately half of the acceleration, while other products, migrations, and workloads also showed robust growth.

Snowflake said it was not ready to share exact consumption-uplift numbers, but that cohort effects were noticeable and the newest customer cohorts were reaching 80% of purchased consumption more visibly.
Snowflake said its forecast was based on observed consumption patterns and raised FY27 product-revenue guidance to $6.07 billion, representing 36% year-over-year growth.

passages.quote: Third, AI activation continues to lift overall platform consumption. Customers using AI on Snowflake consume more across the data platform, creating a structural multiplier for our business.
CoCo— when we look at CoCo, the accounts that are using CoCo are consuming more of the core as well. And so there's this flywheel effect that we talk about.

They contributed approximately half of the acceleration that we are seeing. But there are a lot of other products that are also demonstrating robust growth... And of course, migrations themselves going faster.
At this time, we aren't ready to share the exact uplift numbers, but we do measure cohort behavior.
As always, our forecast is based on observed consumption patterns... For FY27, we now expect product revenue of $6.07 billion, representing 36% year-over-year growth.

caveats: Snowflake did not disclose the exact consumption uplift for AI adopters relative to non-adopters.
The FY27 revenue outlook is management guidance and may change; the call included forward-looking statements.
The most recent available earnings call as of 2026-11-10 was Q2 FY27, held on 2026-09-02; the Q3 FY27 call had not occurred by the stated as-of date.
